hints: For each query interval of time [a,b], only movies fully contained in that interval can be watched.
Sort movies by ending time and precompute the next compatible movie after each one.
Binary lifting lets you jump through the greedy schedule for many selections.
analogy: Answer each time window by repeatedly choosing the earliest-ending movie that fits, using jump pointers to skip many choices.
example: For movies [1,3],[3,5],[5,7], interval [1,6] allows the first two, so answer 2.
algorithm: Sort movies by end time; build successor links to the first movie starting at or after each end. Precompute powers of these links; for each query, find the first movie starting>=a and jump while its end<=b.
correctness: Earliest-finish greedy is optimal for interval scheduling, and each jump table entry composes repeated valid next choices within the query boundary.
complexity: O(n log n+q log n) time and O(n log n) space.
